endpoints.name: Ticket
endpoints.description: One ticket by id, with its full field set including custom fields.

endpoints.name: Tickets
endpoints.description: The service desk tickets, with subject, description, status, priority, urgency, impact, the requester, the agent and group assigned, the category and subcategory, the source, and created, updated and due timestamps. Filterable by a named filter or requester email. NOTE THE CODED COLUMNS: status, priority, source, urgency and impact are all returned as NUMBERS, not labels, and Freshservice fixes their meaning rather than exposing a decoder endpoint -- status 2 is Open, 3 Pending, 4 Resolved, 5 Closed, and priority runs 1 Low to 4 Urgent. A breakdown left as raw integers is unreadable.

endpoints.name: Tickets Requested By ID
endpoints.description: The tickets raised by one requester. Requires a requester id. Equivalent to filtering the ticket list, and the per-person view.

endpoints.name: Custom Ticket Query
endpoints.description: Tickets matching a query in Freshservice's own filter syntax. Requires a query. The only route to arbitrary criteria -- the plain listing supports a few named filters and nothing else -- so most non-trivial ticket questions come through here.

endpoints.name: Ticket Fields
endpoints.description: Every field a ticket can carry, standard and custom, with type, whether required, and for dropdowns the allowed choices. The decoder for custom fields, and the statement of what the account actually records.

endpoints.name: Problem
endpoints.description: One problem by its display id.

endpoints.name: Problems
endpoints.description: Problem records -- the underlying causes behind recurring incidents, in ITIL terms. Carries the same coded status and priority columns as tickets. The link from many tickets to one root cause is what makes this table worth having.

endpoints.name: Problem Fields
endpoints.description: Every field a problem can carry.

endpoints.name: Change
endpoints.description: One change by id.

endpoints.name: Changes
endpoints.description: Change records -- planned modifications to infrastructure, with their risk, impact, planned start and end, and approval state. The ITIL change log; change failure rate is measured from here rather than from tickets.

endpoints.name: Custom Changes Query
endpoints.description: Changes matching a query. Requires a query; the arbitrary-criteria route for changes.

endpoints.name: Change Fields
endpoints.description: Every field a change can carry.

endpoints.name: Release
endpoints.description: One release by its display id.

endpoints.name: Releases
endpoints.description: Release records -- the deployments changes are grouped into. The delivery record above changes.

endpoints.name: Filtered Releases
endpoints.description: Releases restricted to a named filter -- all, my open, deleted, unassigned, completed or incompleted. Requires the filter name.

endpoints.name: Release Fields
endpoints.description: Every field a release can carry.

endpoints.name: Time Entries
endpoints.description: The time logged against one ticket, problem, change or release. Requires the module name and the item id. Effort per item, which the item record itself does not carry -- so cost of support is only answerable through this.

endpoints.name: Task
endpoints.description: The tasks attached to one ticket, problem, change or release. Requires the module name and item id. Sub-work within an item, each with its own status and agent.

endpoints.name: Release Tasks by ID
endpoints.description: The tasks of one release. Requires a release id.

endpoints.name: Agent
endpoints.description: One agent by id, with their name, email, groups and roles.

endpoints.name: Active Agents
endpoints.description: The agents currently active. The working roster; agents who have left remain owners of their historical tickets.

endpoints.name: Agents by Status
endpoints.description: Agents filtered to full-time or occasional. Requires the status. Occasional agents share a licence pool, which is why a headcount and a licence count differ.

endpoints.name: User by ID
endpoints.description: One requester by id.

endpoints.name: Users
endpoints.description: The requesters -- the people who raise tickets, as opposed to the agents who work them. Optionally filtered by a query. In Freshservice these are two different tables, so a count of people in the system is the sum of both.

endpoints.name: Department
endpoints.description: One department by id.

endpoints.name: Departments
endpoints.description: The departments requesters belong to, with their heads and domains. The organisational dimension ticket volume is broken down by.

endpoints.name: Asset CI Types
endpoints.description: The asset type hierarchy -- the classes assets belong to, each with its parent. Types are account-specific and nested, so an asset's own fields depend on its type.

endpoints.name: Asset CI Type Fields
endpoints.description: The fields defined for one asset type. Requires the asset type id. THE DECODER for type-specific asset fields, which differ entirely between a laptop and a database service.

endpoints.name: Asset
endpoints.description: One asset by its display id, with its type-specific fields.

endpoints.name: Assets
endpoints.description: The configuration items in the CMDB -- hardware, software, services -- with their asset type, display id, impact, usage and assignment. THE ITSM SIDE THAT TICKETS ATTACH TO: a ticket about a failing laptop is only connectable to that laptop through here.

endpoints.name: Asset Search
endpoints.description: Assets matching a search query. Requires the query.

endpoints.name: Relationship Types
endpoints.description: The relationship types defined, each with its forward and reverse names. The decoder for the direction of a relationship, which the relationship record only references.

endpoints.name: Relationships
endpoints.description: The relationships one asset has to others -- depends on, connected to, hosted on. Requires the asset display id. The CMDB's graph, and what makes impact analysis possible: which services a failing server takes down is only answerable here.

endpoints.name: Solution Category
endpoints.description: One knowledge base category by id.

endpoints.name: Solution Folders
endpoints.description: The folders within one category. Requires the folder id.

endpoints.name: Solution Categories
endpoints.description: The top level of the knowledge base.

endpoints.name: Solution Article
endpoints.description: One article by id, with its body.

endpoints.name: Solution Articles
endpoints.description: The knowledge base articles in one folder, with title, status and view counts. Requires a folder id. The self-service content whose use is what deflects tickets.

endpoints.name: Service Items
endpoints.description: Every item in the service catalogue, with name, description, cost and delivery time. What can be requested, and the cost figure is one of the few monetary values Freshservice holds.

endpoints.name: Service Categories
endpoints.description: The categories of the service catalogue -- the requestable services, as opposed to the incidents in the ticket table.

endpoints.name: Service Category Items
endpoints.description: The catalogue items within one category. Requires a category id.

endpoints.name: Service Item
endpoints.description: One catalogue item by its display id, with its request fields.

endpoints.name: Contract
endpoints.description: One contract by its display id.

endpoints.name: Contracts
endpoints.description: The support and licence contracts recorded, with vendor, cost, start and expiry dates, and the assets covered. Contract expiry is the usual reason this table is consulted, and it is not derivable from the assets themselves.
